Definition: properly, to stare at (compare G3700), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear:--behold, perceive, see, take heed.
BiblicalUsage: The plain sense of horáō is behold, perceive, see, take heed. It comes up 453 times, and the passages from John, Matthew, Hebrews, and 3 John show how steadily Scripture uses it. I do not find a second, secret meaning hiding behind it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that horáō matters because seeing God is the promise held out to the pure in heart. I read this as a reminder that God’s words mean what they say, and I can trust them.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Moses' Birth and Flight to Midian; Diotrephes Refuses the Brethren
